broccoli:

So, the real question is…do those of us at the launch party WAIT to post rules question until others have received their copies? OR should we start asking questions right away, to confuse, confound, and make jealous those that are still waiting?

I have actually been considering this for quite awhile. Vengeance will be released in waves, which is going to give different people, thourhg no fault of their own, knowledge of the game at different times. Therefore, I don't think it's a good idea for people to randomly mention diffrent things before most people had a chance to get the game. There are many people who like to be surprised, and they shouldn't have to avoid this site, just because of the way the game is ebing released.

As we get closer, I was going to create 2 threads. One for general stuff, and another for rules. I thought it would be a great idea to limit all discussion of Vengeance in these forums, to just those thread. This way, people can still enjoy the community, without having to worry about spoilers. If they want to be spoiled, they can read those threads, but it should be there option.

If GtG is onboard with the idea, I (or anyone else) will create those threads with topics that warn about the spoilers.

posts.cooked:
We beg and beg the game developers to give us clues and previews of the upcoming expansions, and then when the game is released we ask players not to say anything until we get our copies...

I kind of agree.  Why not let people jabber about the exciting upcoming product?  Because some people don't have it yet?  Lots of people won't be buying it immediately, so even a year after it's fully available the problem would be the same.  Seems to me, once the product has been sent to the printer, it's out of beta.  Time to lift the beta/playtesting NDA and let people tell the world the glorious news about what's coming.

Better yet would be for >G to do an info offensive as soon as the product goes to the printer so that they controlled the flow of exciting new info in the lead-up to release, but that seems to be either too time consuming or not interesting enough to them to do.

Sure, there's a correlation, but a card game isn't a movie or a book.  If someone says "omigod, NewGuyHero has this one card that does XYZ, wihch makes him wicked vs. SuperHardVillainMan", is that the same thing as knowing that Bruce Willis was dead the whole time (sorry, spoiler) which is the lynchpin of the entire movie?  I would argue that any info you hear before packages appears on doorsteps is just going to get people pumped about getting their hands on NewGuyHero, not ruin your enjoyment of the game.

I mean, what is there to spoil?  We know what the heroes are, we know what the villains are, we have a general idea of how Vengeance changes the gameplay.  Does it really matter if we know what the text is on any particular new card?  How would this be any different than for people who have to wait to get Vengeance until next X-mas because they don't have the money for it now?  They're going to be bombarded with spoilers all year, but that's different and OK I guess?
